name: exec
description: Execute, observe, and cancel bounded non-interactive Linux /bin/bash processes.

exec.description: Execute one bounded non-interactive Linux /bin/bash command. The explicit cwd must resolve inside agent work or the configured workspace; `.` means the agent-work root and `workspace/...` selects the workspace. The shell itself runs with the runtime process permissions and is not an operating-system sandbox. A command still running after the foreground window yields a process ID and cursor that exec_wait can resume without restarting it. Prefer dedicated inspection and file-mutation capabilities when they can express the task.

execute_command.summary: Execute one bounded non-interactive Linux /bin/bash command in an explicit existing agent-work or workspace directory. The cwd boundary is not an OS sandbox. Full-access availability does not authorize servers, GUI automation, installs, service changes, background work, or other sensitive effects.

exec_wait.description: Continue observing the exact running shell process returned by exec. Use only the process ID and next cursor from the latest exec or exec_wait result. This does not start the command again.

wait_for_process.summary: Wait for the next bounded observation from one running exec process without restarting it.

exec_cancel.description: Cancel one running shell process previously returned by exec. Use only when the current task no longer needs that process or the user asks to stop it.

cancel_process.summary: Stop one active exec process and report its final state.
